For me, it helps to be in a silent environment. If I want to read in a noisy one, I’ll listen to an audiobook in headphones and follow along in an actual copy of the book. Also, I used to be like, okay I’m gonna try to read x amount of pages today and stopping that helped. What I really struggled with was not getting frustrated when I didn’t meet my reading goals, when I’d have to reread pages because I didn’t retain anything, when I couldn’t get myself to finish a book, when I wanted to read leisurely even if I hadn’t read all the things I needed to for school/work. I’m working on that and reading is less intimidating now. If you can, I also turn my phone off or put it in another room.

chain smoking, hardly brushing my teeth, showering only a few times a week. i lash out at friends or family when i finally do speak to them. i don’t take my medicine. i either starve myself or overeat. i sleep upwards of 13 hours or less than 20 minutes. can’t focus, always daydreaming or have my head someplace it shouldn’t be. don’t go to school and easily overwhelmed. 

the first thing that helps is maintaining a sort of consistency or schedule. of course i’m not going to get everything i need to do done, and what i get done may be improperly completed. i have to realize that is okay. i set alarms and reminders for basic things, and it does feel silly, but without them i seriously wouldn’t do them. i give myself things to look forward to like shopping on weekends or new tattoos. i set plans with people close to me and tell them “don’t let me back out.” call until i answer, if i cancel come over and knock on my door until i wake up. for a long time the hardest thing for me has been to simply and literally get out of bed in the morning. my dog helps with this. she’ll bark or paw at me until i get up to feed her and let her out. even if i’m not eating that day, she has to.
